summary: v1.8 scheduler feature: full CRUD + validation + end-to-end dispatch tested via pytest (12/12 passing including 90s live dispatch), plus UI flow via Playwright — sidebar nav, create schedule with cron template, toggle pause/resume, delete. Regressions on prior v16/v17 test suites: 21/22 passing (only failure is v16 stale version assertion 1.5.0 vs 1.8.0 — pre-existing, unrelated).
action_items: Optional: update /app/backend/tests/test_v16_launch.py::test_root_version stale assertion (expects 1.5.0, backend now returns 1.8.0) — cosmetic housekeeping only.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/schedules.py PATCH: when caller updates only 'cron' but the schedule is disabled, next_run_at is correctly forced to null (good). When re-enabling without a cron change, next_run_at is set — correct.
services/scheduler.py: 20s tick is fine for minute-level cron; sub-minute schedules would be missed but that's out of scope (min cron granularity is 1 min).
scheduler _tick fallback on exception disables the schedule — good hot-loop guard.
SchedulerPage delete has no confirmation dialog; consider a confirm for destructive action.
seed_data_creation: None (tests self-clean by delete or use unique users).
context_for_next_testing_agent: v1.8 adds POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/schedules + background scheduler loop (tick=20s) that fires enqueue_scheduled_scan and stamps last_run_at + last_scan_id. Dispatch end-to-end verified with cron '* * * * *' within ~60-90s. Frontend Scheduler page at /scheduler with data-testids: nav-scheduler, scheduler-page, schedule-name-input, schedule-target-input, schedule-cron-input, cron-template-0..4, create-schedule-button, schedule-item-{id}, schedule-toggle-{id}, schedule-delete-{id}, schedule-count.
